facts.statement: Iberospinus was an extinct spinosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) in Portugal.
facts.quote: Iberospinus (meaning "Iberian spine") is an extinct genus of spinosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Papo Seco Formation of Portugal.

facts.statement: The first fossil material of Iberospinus was discovered in 1999, followed by expeditions between 2004 and 2008.
facts.quote: The first fossil material was discovered in 1999, with additional expeditions from 2004 to 2008.

facts.statement: Specimen ML1190 was originally described as a Baryonyx in 2011 but was later identified as a unique species in 2019.
facts.quote: After being described as a specimen of Baryonyx in 2011, it was realised to have been a unique species in 2019, with specimen ML1190 as the holotype.

facts.statement: Iberospinus is known from a collection of bones including jaw fragments, teeth, a scapula, vertebrae, ribs, a pubis, calcanea, and a foot bone.
facts.quote: Iberospinus is currently known from dentary fragments, teeth, an incomplete right scapula, partial dorsal and caudal vertebrae, rib fragments, a partial pubis, two incomplete calcanea, and a pedal ungual phalanx.

facts.statement: All known fossil material of Iberospinus belongs to a single individual.
facts.quote: All of the material belongs to one individual.

facts.statement: The name Iberospinus combines "Iberia" for its location and "spine" referring to the elongated neural spines of related dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Of the generic name, "Iberospinus," "ibero" is derived from Iberia, a Roman name for the Iberian Peninsula, while the Latin spinus means spine, after the elongated neural spines of related spinosaurids.

facts.statement: The species name natarioi honors Carlos Natário, who discovered the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name, "natarioi" honors Carlos Natário, the discoverer of the holotype.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Iberospinus possessed an intricate neurovascular system connecting the teeth to external openings.
facts.quote: The dentary (lower jaw) of Iberospinus shows an intricate neurovascular system that would connect the teeth and the external foramina.

facts.statement: A series of replacement teeth were preserved in the lower jaw of Iberospinus.
facts.quote: A series of replacement teeth are also preserved in the dentary.

facts.statement: Bone characteristics in the tail and foot suggest Iberospinus may have had a semi-aquatic lifestyle, though lacking extreme adaptations seen in other spinosaurines.
facts.quote: Characteristics of the bones, especially in the tail and pedal ungual phalanx, indicate a possible semi-aquatic lifestyle, though the extreme features in some related spinosaurines are not seen.

facts.statement: The lower jaw bone of Iberospinus has a straight bottom edge and a single opening in the Meckelian groove, unlike the curved edges of most other spinosaurids.
facts.quote: The dentary bone contains a single foramen within the Meckelian sulcus and has a straight ventral edge instead of curved as in most other spinosaurids.

facts.statement: The shoulder blade of Iberospinus features a straight front edge without a protruding acromion and a coracoid contact covering the entire bottom surface.
facts.quote: The scapula has a straight anterior rim without a protruding acromion and a coracoidal contact occupying the entire ventral surface.

facts.statement: The pubic bone of Iberospinus has a thick apron along its entire shaft and a mound-like bump on the upper outer side.
facts.quote: The pubic apron is thick throughout the entire length of the pubic shaft. There is a mound-like eminence in the proximal lateral portion of the pubic bone.

facts.statement: In 2019, researchers placed Iberospinus within Spinosauridae but outside the subfamilies Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: In 2019, Arden et al. recovered it as a spinosaurid outside of the Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Iberospinus may be closely related to Baryonychinae because the fossils show certain characteristics of that group.
facts.quote: However, they explain that the fossil material shows some characteristics of baryonychines, suggesting a closer relation to the group.

facts.statement: A 2025 study concluded that Iberospinus is the earliest diverging member of Spinosaurinae, ruling out the possibility that it is the same species as Camarillasaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2025 reassessment of Camarillasaurus, Rauhut and colleagues recovered Iberospinus as the basalmost member of the Spinosaurinae, with Camarillasaurus as a later-diverging taxon, precluding their synonymization.

facts.statement: A 2017 study determined that the holotype specimen died between 23 and 25 years old, near its maximum size and skeletal maturity.
facts.quote: A 2017 histological study of growth lines by the German palaeontologist Katja Waskow and Mateus found that specimen ML1190 had died between the age of 23 and 25 years old, and was close to its maximum size and skeletal maturity.

facts.statement: Iberospinus reached sexual maturity between 13 and 15 years old, indicated by a slowdown in its growth rate.
facts.quote: The study also found that the animal had reached sexual maturity at the age of 13 to 15 years, due to a decrease in growth rate at this point.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that juvenile traits retained in adults (paedomorphosis) in Iberospinus may have aided swimming locomotion.
facts.quote: Paedomorphic traits may be related to swimming locomotion, as they have been suggested in other extinct animals thought to have been aquatic (such as plesiosaurs and temnospondyls).

facts.statement: Iberospinus lived in a lagoon environment represented by marl rocks in the Papo Seco Formation of Portugal.
facts.quote: The Papo Seco Formation of Portugal where Iberospinus is known from is composed of marl, representing a lagoon environment.

facts.statement: Scratches on the bones of Iberospinus may be bite marks left by small scavengers.
facts.quote: Most of the bones of Iberospinus specimen ML1190 were damaged, and some scratches may be marks from small scavengers.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Iberospinus died on land and its bones were transported to the lagoon environment where they were found.
facts.quote: The specimen's disarticulation indicates it was transported from a more-terrestrial environment (since many bones are missing), but those found were close together.

facts.statement: Iberospinus is classified within the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Iberospinus lived during the Early Cretaceous, between 129 and 125 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
